note: One entry per screenshot on plantoir.app. `build.py` reads alt and caption to write the <picture> element; `website/shots/capture.py` reads `capture` to know how each is produced. Every shot is taken twice, once with the Mac in light appearance and once in dark, and saved as site/img/<id>-light.png and -dark.png. Paths are lowercase because Quartz serves lowercase URLs and 301s anything else — a capitalised address would be photographed mid-redirect. Since v1.4.0: `capture.scene` names the scene in capture.py that makes the shot (`capture.py --only <scene>`); `capture.workspace` says which working folder it is taken in ('marketing' = ~/Plantoir Marketing, ICS3U; 'demo' = ~/Desktop/Teaching, the three published demo courses); `expectText` lists words the finished picture must show, read back with Vision text recognition, so a picture of the wrong state fails its scene; `awaiting_capture` marks a shot the pages already name whose capture waits for the release it photographs (build.py renders nothing for it meanwhile); `waiting_on: "#<issue>"` beside it names the GitHub issue a capture waits on for a reason that is not the release — `--deploy` lets such a shot through, and the capture removes both flags; `windows: true` marks the ids capture_windows.py also takes; `windows: false` marks a scene Windows does not have yet, so its visitors are shown the Mac picture and any older `-windows` file is ignored (since 2026-10-04 no id is false: every picture has its Windows twin, #380). `windowsAlt` is the alt text for the Windows picture where the shared one names something only the Mac picture shows; base.html swaps it in as it swaps the image, and a Mac visitor's words never change. `static: true` marks a figure that is one image (`<id>.png`) rather than a light/dark pair; `dark: true` beside it says the figure ALSO has a Dark Mode version, `<id>-dark.png`/`.webp`, which a page in dark mode is given (`<id>.png` stays the light one, so its name never changes; build.py reports it missing as a problem).

shots.alt: Three overlapping windows in a diagonal cascade: Markdown notes in Obsidian on the left, Plantoir deploying the site in the middle, and the finished class website in Safari on the right.
shots.caption: From your notes in Obsidian, through Plantoir, to a live class website.
shots.windowsAlt: Three overlapping windows in a diagonal cascade: Markdown notes in Obsidian on the left, Plantoir deploying the site in the middle, and the finished class website in Edge on the right.

shots.alt: The Plantoir window: ICS3U and ICS4U in the sidebar, last year's ICS3U filed under Reference Courses, and ICS3U's settings open beside them.
shots.caption: Every course you teach, and last year's beside them.

shots.alt: The New Course panel with TEJ3M entered and its suggested course names offered beneath.
shots.caption: A course code is enough to start.

shots.alt: A progress view describing, in plain language, the step the site build has reached.
shots.caption: Progress is described in words, not in log output.

shots.alt: The Plantoir window with a class website shown inside it, beside the list of courses and sections.
shots.caption: The site, in the app, before anyone else has seen it.

shots.alt: The assistant window: a request typed in plain English, and the assistant describing what it is about to change with a button to approve it.
shots.caption: It says what it will do, then waits.

shots.alt: A Grade 10 English class website in a browser, with a navigation sidebar, a search field and a page of class notes.
shots.caption: What a class sees.

shots.alt: A Grade 12 Calculus and Vectors page opening with typeset mathematics: a displayed definition and a table of derivative rules.
shots.caption: The preview is the real site — equations and all.

shots.alt: A Grade 11 Chemistry class page with two balanced reactions set on lines of their own, states in brackets and subscripts set low, and the sulfate and ammonium ions written with their charges.
shots.caption: Chemistry too: formulas, charges, states and reaction arrows, set the way a textbook sets them.

shots.alt: A Grade 11 Chemistry page showing a flowchart beside the few lines of text that produced it.
shots.caption: Diagrams are written, not drawn — and edited in seconds.

shots.alt: The same class website at phone width, with the navigation collapsed behind a button.
shots.caption: The same site on a phone.

shots.alt: A grid of every curriculum expectation in a course, each square shaded by how many pages address it, with pale squares showing the gaps.
shots.caption: Every expectation in the course, shaded by how well it is covered.

shots.alt: A search panel open over a class website, listing matching pages with the search term highlighted in context.
shots.caption: One box, the whole course.

shots.alt: Three class websites overlapping like a fanned deck of cards, each in a different colour scheme and typeface.
shots.caption: Three courses, three colour schemes. Chosen in the app, not in code.

shots.alt: The same class website twice, side by side: once in a light colour scheme and once in a dark one.
shots.caption: And every site does both, whichever a student prefers.

shots.alt: The Schedule Deploy sheet for ICS3U Section 1 set for a morning time, with a macOS notification above it saying the section published on its own.
shots.caption: Set it on Sunday. Hear how it went on Monday.
shots.windowsAlt: The Plantoir window with the Schedule a deploy sheet for ICS3U Section 1 set for a morning time; when the deploy has run, Windows tells the teacher how it went with a notification.

shots.alt: The Plantoir sidebar with last year's ICS3U under Reference Courses, 2025–26, and a sheet about to copy one of its pages into ICS4U, with "Also copy the pages this page links to" ticked.
shots.caption: Last year's course, to read and borrow from — never published.

shots.alt: The Get Ready for the Start of the Year sheet for ICS3U Section 2, listing the classes and pages it will put into draft, with a reason beside each.
shots.caption: Every class after Day 1 into draft, with the reasons, before you agree.

shots.alt: Two curriculum coverage maps for the same ICS3U section: the Ontario expectations, and the AP Computer Science Principles learning objectives, each shaded by how many pages reach it.
shots.caption: Two curricula, a map for each.

shots.alt: ICS3U's Course Settings with both the Curriculum folder and the College Board Curriculum folder ticked as curricula.
shots.caption: Tick a folder, and it gets a map.

shots.alt: A class activity page whose curriculum connection quotes an Ontario expectation and an AP learning objective, one under the other.
shots.caption: One lesson, counted on both maps.

shots.alt: Obsidian open on ICS3U's How I Teach page: short notes on units, assessment and classroom routines.
shots.caption: Tell Claude or Codex how you teach, once. It is never published.

shots.alt: The New Course or Club panel with CODING entered and "This is a club" switched on, explaining that a club's pages are numbered one after another, it has no curriculum, and it starts with a page for its first meeting.
shots.caption: Clubs start the way clubs do.
